title: 1 Samuel 22:1–5
context: David escapes to the cave of Adullam, where his family joins him along with a band of distressed, indebted, and discontented men, about four hundred in all, with David as their captain. He secures a refuge for his parents with the king of Moab. Then the prophet Gad directs him back into the land of Judah.

verses.text: David therefore departed from there and escaped to Adullam’s cave. When his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, they went down there to him.
verses.arminianNotes: David escapes to Adullam's cave, and his family comes to him. Arminian readers see God providing companionship in hardship. WEB’s heading to Psalm 142 is, “A contemplation by David, when he was in the cave. A Prayer.” Psalm 57’s heading likewise places that prayer “when he fled from Saul, in the cave.”
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Adullam was a town in Judah's lowland (Joshua 15:35). The anointed king's first gathering point is a cave, and God begins forming his future kingdom in obscurity and weakness.

verses.text: Everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented gathered themselves to him; and he became captain over them. There were with him about four hundred men.
verses.arminianNotes: The distressed, indebted, and discontented gather to David, about four hundred men. Arminian readers see a ragged community drawn to a leader who welcomes them, and their real choice to follow him into hardship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that God builds David's following from the overlooked and burdened. Many see in this a pattern of God choosing the weak, though they caution against reading every detail as a symbol.

verses.text: David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother come out to you, until I know what God will do for me.”
verses.arminianNotes: David asks the king of Moab to shelter his parents "until I know what God will do for me." Arminian readers see honest uncertainty joined to trust, waiting on God while acting responsibly for his family.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note David's confidence that God has a purpose for him, even if he does not yet know it. Some point to David's Moabite ancestry through Ruth (Ruth 4:17) as a possible reason for seeking refuge in Moab.

verses.text: He brought them before the king of Moab; and they lived with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
verses.arminianNotes: David's parents live with the king of Moab while David is in the stronghold. Arminian readers note David's care for his father and mother as a real expression of faithfulness, keeping the command to honor parents.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God's provision extending beyond Israel's borders. A foreign king shelters the parents of the coming king, a reminder that God's care for his chosen line is not limited by nation.

verses.text: The prophet Gad said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold. Depart, and go into the land of Judah.” Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hereth.
verses.arminianNotes: The prophet Gad tells David to leave the stronghold and go into Judah. Arminian readers see David responding obediently to God's word through the prophet, even though Judah means greater danger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the first appearance of Gad, later called "David's seer" (2 Samuel 24:11). God guides his anointed through his word, and David's obedience places him back in the land God promised.
